business_scope.primary_industry_name: Customs Clearance Brokerage and Bonded Transit Management

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law rooted in German-influenced Commercial Code, with modernized statutory corporate and AML/CFT frameworks; not a pure Common Law jurisdiction, nor Sharia; the Supreme Court of Korea and Constitutional Court provide binding precedent within the statutory framework)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement Between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (China-ROK BIT, signed 1992, entered into force 1992, as amended through 2007)

Convention Between the Republic of Korea and the People's Republic of Korea for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (Korea-China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement, signed 1994, as amended by Protocol 2007)
Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (RCEP, Korea as a signatory, entered into force for Korea on 1 February 2022)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as most recently amended, including Article 5ter obligating financial companies to identify and verify the ultimate beneficial owner); Financial Transaction Reports Act; Act on the Regulation of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds; Act on the Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) regulations; Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism; Act on Corporate Governance of Commercial Companies (Korean Commercial Code, Act No. 1000, as amended, Book IV, registration of a Chusik Hoesa requiring shareholder and beneficial owner identification); Customs Act, Articles 88 and 315 concerning the licensing of customs brokers and enhanced UBO transparency for licensed customs brokerage entities; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality; Act on the Protection of Personal Information; and the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) mutual evaluation follow-up measures adopted by the Republic of Korea.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Chusik Hoesa Incorporation Registration Certificate, official extract from the Korean Commercial Registration Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Clerk of the District Court (Local District Court Registration Department) upon registration of incorporation; official extract issued by the Court Registration Office of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention path for Apostille member states: (i) official seal and signature of the District Court clerk, (ii) verification of the official signature at the Seoul High Court or the National Court Administration, Ministry of Court Administration, (iii) issuance of an Apostille certificate by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA, Apostille Division) of the Republic of Korea, and (iv) submission to the receiving foreign authority in the destination Apostille member state. For non-Apostille states: (i) District Court clerk signature, (ii) examination by MOFA, (iii) submission to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for consular legalization certification, and (iv) final legalization by the consular or embassy official of the non-member receiving state accredited in Korea. Never chain both procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (법인등기사항증명서 confirming no dissolution, merger, or encumbrance, issued within 30 days before submission)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office (Court Registry Office), Republic of Korea, under the Court Registration Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Apostille states: (i) court registration officer's signature, (ii) signature authentication by the relevant District Court or High Court, (iii) Apostille certificate from MOFA; Consular legalization for non-Apostille states: (i) signature verification at the Ministry of Court Administration, (ii) MOFA authentication, and (iii) consular legalization by the destination country's embassy in Seoul. These are mutually exclusive paths; no sequential stacking.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the foreign incorporation agent and appointing the local registered address agent, with attested copy of the minutes and a copy of each director's identification document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The board of directors of the Chusik Hoesa applicant/formation company as recorded in the notarial minute record prepared by a licensed Korean notary public or, where made abroad, by the notarial office of the country of origin, followed by consular or apostille authentication in the origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Korean-origin document to be used abroad: (i) notarization before a Korean notary public (or an attorney-at-law authorized under the Notarial Practice Act), (ii) authentication of the notary's seal at the relevant District Court, (iii) Apostille certificate by MOFA. For a foreign-origin document to be used in Korea: (i) notarization in the origin country, (ii) Apostille certificate if the origin country is an Apostille member, or (iii) consular legalization at the Korean Embassy in the origin country if the origin country is not an Apostille member. Mutually exclusive paths, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jeong-kwan, 정관) duly executed and notarized, including share class, transfer restrictions, and UBO nominee prohibitions, filed with the District Court upon incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The incorporators, a certified legal specialist attorney, and the notary public for verification; official copy from the District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Apostille member state recipients: (i) notarization, (ii) District Court signature certification, (iii) MOFA Apostille. Consular legalization for non-member states: (i) District Court certification, (ii) MOFA certificate, (iii) legalization by the consulate of the destination state. The paths are alternative and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by a licensed Korean bank confirming the opening of the provisional USD/KRW corporate account, the identification of an authorized signer, and the verification of the UBO under Article 5ter of the Specific Financial Information Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed banking institution in the Republic of Korea subject to KoFIU supervision under the Financial Services Commission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: (i) seal confirmation of the bank's representative director at the notary, (ii) certificate of signature ratification by the banking supervision division of the Financial Supervisory Service, (iii) MOFA Apostille. Consular path: (i) verification of bank executive signature by the financial authorities, (ii) MOFA authentication, and (iii) legalization by the embassy of the destination country in Korea. Only one path applies depending on the destination country's treaty status; never apply both.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the consolidated OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN) as updated daily, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) sanctions and suspicious transaction report (STR) guidance, the Korean government's sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Act on the Prohibition of Financial Transactions with Foreign Country, and the domestic PEP list maintained by the Financial Services Commission and KoFIU under the Specific Financial Information Act. Every proposed director, substantial shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, customs brokerage licensed officer, and signatory must undergo an initial adverse media and PEP check, a transnational politically exposed person determination including immediate family and close associates under a risk-based enhanced due diligence framework, and continuous transaction monitoring using risk scoring for shell company indicators, nominee shareholding red flags, and sanctions evasion typologies, with a minimum 5-year retention of KYC records and immediate STR filing under Article 4 of the Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information. The protocol must apply the 25% ownership threshold, and additionally, for a licensed customs brokerage under the Customs Act, the Korea Customs Service requires full UBO disclosure at any percentage and confirmation of no bankruptcy, criminal tax conviction, or customs fraud record under Article 88 of the Customs Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (인터넷등기소), the official electronic company name clearance and registration portal operated by the Supreme Court of Korea; alternative portal: the Commercial Registration E-Government System of the Court Registry Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chusik Hoesa must adopt a Hangul statutory name under the Korean Commercial Code. The registered name must be written in Korean characters; however, a foreign language name may be registered as an additional trade name through the commercial registration system. The transliteration doctrine applies when the desired foreign name is converted into Hangul using the Revised Romanization of Korean or the statutory Hangul equivalence, ensuring that the registered Hangul name does not cause deception or confusion with existing registered names under Article 18 of the Commercial Code. Four-tier naming conventions: (1) the enterprise identifier using a descriptive Hangul or fully transliterated foreign term, (2) the business classification portion clearly indicating a customs brokerage or freight forwarding related purpose, (3) the entity suffix '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa), and (4) the additional foreign-language trade name clause, included in the articles of association as an appended trade name, which requires separate name clearance against the registry's foreign-name search field. The name clearance doctrine prohibits identical or deceptively similar names in Hangul and also protects famous trade names registered with KIPO under the Unfair Competition Prevention Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant shall request a written rejection rationale from the registry officer. Within seven days of the stated rejection, an administrative appeal must be lodged with the head of the competent District Court Registration Office, accompanied by a formal written statement setting forth the grounds of distinctiveness, the prior trademark search result from KIPO, and a legal comparison under Article 18 of the Commercial Code and the Unfair Competition Prevention Act. The filing party may also petition for a reconsideration hearing and present evidence of actual use, intended geographic scope, and the absence of consumer confusion. If the registry maintains the rejection, a judicial appeal shall be filed with the High Court within fourteen days of the notice, and a preliminary name reservation may be renewed for a subsequent period until the final judgment. Simultaneously, counsel should submit one or two alternative names in the same filing to secure clearance. Should the registry err in an arbitrary rejection, the applicant may claim compensation under the State Compensation Act. All appeals and filings must be processed in the Korean language, and where required, accompanied by notarized English translations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or post-office box number is not permissible for a Chusik Hoesa serving as a licensed customs brokerage house. Both the National Tax Service and the Korea Customs Service require that the registered office be a physical, identifiable address within the jurisdiction, capable of receiving official postal items, inspection teams, and administrative summons. The Korean Commercial Code and the Customs Act require that the head office location be a fixed commercial premises, with tangible facilities, local personnel, and operational records kept on site. A virtual office may be tolerated for ancillary administrative use only if it provides a dedicated physical conference room, a full-time office manager under a lease agreement, and the obligation to accept unannounced registry and tax inspection notices; however, banks applying AML enhanced due diligence normally decline an entity whose registered address is merely a virtual mailbox, particularly in the licensed customs brokerage sector. The Korea Customs Service requires the actual place of business to be a site where the customs broker performs his duties, maintains confidential importer records, and can produce books and records in an on-site examination. Therefore, the safe requirement is a physical office lease in the entity's name, outfitted to sustain customs clearance business operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist and quantified risk: (1) National Tax Service routine tax verification: 30% within the first fiscal year for a newly incorporated brokerage; (2) unannounced customs inspection by the Korea Customs Service under Article 315 of the Customs Act: 65% within the first two years, especially where the company operates bonded transit or ACH Broker Interface transactions; (3) district-level commercial registry physical attendance and signboard verification: 35% annually; (4) Financial Services Commission/KoFIU delegated on-site AML audit in relation to the bank and payment rail ACH usage: 20% in the first year due to Medium-Risk classification. Checklist items: an actual signboard bearing the registered corporate name, the licensed customs broker's nameplate and employment contract, a physically present customs broker or staff, the original lease and utility invoices in the company name, the corporate seal and bank documents stored on site, the availability of computer systems connected to UNI-PASS, and a formal-file archive for customs declarations for at least five years. An unannounced inspection by the Korea Customs Service may be conducted without prior notice under Article 316 of the Customs Act. A virtual mailbox in this industry is an unacceptable shell risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 288, 289, 291, 295, 300, 317 and 329; Registration of Incorporation Rules of the Supreme Court of Korea; Customs Act of Korea, Article 113, for customs clearance brokerage licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered head office, served through the Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (iRO) and the court registry business window.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) filed under Article 317 of the Commercial Act and the Registration of Non-Contentious Cases Rules of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Since the 2012 amendment of Article 329(3) of the Commercial Act, no statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa. The paid-up capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation, regardless of amount, must be deposited into a blocked capital subscription account held in the corporation's tentative name at a licensed Korean commercial bank, and funds may not be withdrawn until the notarized Articles of Incorporation and incorporation registration are accepted by the competent court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IN RE: KR_CHUSIKHOESA, a joint stock company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. WHEREAS the incorporators have subscribed to the whole of the authorized ordinary shares of the Corporation and have convened the statutory organizational meeting; and WHEREAS the board now intends to fix the corporate governance and financial operating structure, to establish authorised bank accounts, to adopt a physical registered office in the Republic of Korea, and to appoint qualified officers capable of discharging customs brokerage duties; and WHEREAS the board has reviewed and approved the capital subscription arrangements and has verified that all subscribed paid-in capital has been deposited in the Corporation's name in a blocked capital subscription account at a commercial bank, subject to withdrawal restrictions imposed by Korean law until the registration of the Corporation is complete. NOW, THEREFORE, be it RESOLVED by the Board of Directors of the Corporation as follows: 1. RESOLVED, that the total issued ordinary shares of the Corporation are hereby subscribed, allotted and ratified in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. The board acknowledges that the shareholders have paid the full amount of the called subscription price, and the board directs the corporate secretary to cause proper entries to be made in the share capital register. 2. RESOLVED, that the representative director and one other director, or the representative director together with the corporate seal custodian appointed by the representative director, are hereby authorised, jointly and severally, to open ordinary deposit accounts, foreign currency trust accounts and customs broker settlement accounts with such banks as the Corporation may select, to sign account mandates, to execute electronic banking agreements, to wire funds for customs duties and excise taxes, and to give indemnities in favour of the bankers. Any one of the authorised officers may act where the relevant bank mandate so permits. 3. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation shall be situated at the physical address stated in the Articles of Incorporation and in the corporate registry. The board authorises the payment of rent, telecommunications, data, maintenance, legal compliance and utility expenses, and directs the officers to maintain all corporate records, seals, statutory registers and customs brokerage records at such registered office. 4. RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed by the board to serve at the pleasure of the board: the representative director and president, the managing director for customs brokerage operations, the finance director and the corporate secretary. Where any such officer is licensed as a customs broker under Article 113 of the Customs Act, that person shall be designated as the responsible licensed customs broker and shall supervise all import, export and bonded transit filings. 5. RESOLVED, that the board adopts an external auditor where required by law, and that no director, officer or shareholder may take action contrary to the court's order of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Articles of Incorporation and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (iRO) and a licensed Korean notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search on the iRO portal using the proposed Korean trade name and its Romanized equivalent. Submit a name reservation application and select a permissible corporate objective covering customs clearance brokerage, import and export agency, bonded transit management and related advisory services, so that the registered purpose does not conflict with the Customs Act. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation with at least one incorporator and one or more directors. Have the Articles notarized by a Korean notary public to confirm the legality of the founders' intent and the accuracy of all statements regarding shares, office address and governance. Verify that a physical office is located in the court district where registration will be filed and that the future customs broker workplace can satisfy document retention requirements.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation application
Passport or alien identification of each incorporator
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean and English
English translation affidavit if documents are bilingual
Power of attorney appointing local counsel for foreign incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or confusingly similar, file an amended name reservation with the iRO; if the notary requests corrections, amend the articles and re-notarize; if the registry later queries the purpose clause, revise the purpose to include only lawful brokerage activities and submit an explanatory note.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Account Deposit and Foreign Investment Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission and, where applicable, Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a designated foreign exchange bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Articles are notarized, open a temporary capital subscription account at a licensed bank under the tentative name of the corporation. Deposit all subscription funds by wire or cash and obtain the bank's certificate of deposit stating the corporation name, amount, account number and date of deposit. For non-resident investors, the remitter must identify beneficial ownership and, where the overseas investor will hold ten percent or more, file a foreign investment proposal with a foreign exchange bank or KOTRA before payment. Do not transfer funds out of the capital subscription account until the court has registered the corporation, because the Commercial Act treats the account as restricted for the protection of creditors during the formation process.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital subscription minutes
Bank capital subscription account certificate
Foreign exchange transaction confirmation if remitted from overseas
Foreign investment declaration or report certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, provide audited bank statements and investor background information; if the foreign exchange report is rejected, correct the ownership and remittance data and resubmit; if funds are returned, redeposit using a complying remitter and amend the foreign investment report with KOTRA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered head office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the statutory incorporation registration with the district court for the location of the registered head office within fourteen to twenty-one days after the capital subscription deposit. Use the official registration form for incorporation of a stock corporation and pay the registration tax and local education tax according to the court's tariff. Attach the notarized Articles, the bank certificate of deposit, written consents of the directors and auditor if any, and valid identification of the representative directors. The registry officer verifies that the company has a lawful purpose and at least one director, that the capital subscription is genuine, and that the registered office address is physically valid. Once registered, the court issues the corporate register extract and accepts the filing of the corporate seal. The corporate seal certificate is then used for banking, tax and customs filings.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital subscription deposit
Written acceptance of appointment by each director and auditor
Identification documents of directors and incorporators
Corporate seal registration application after incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction request, amend the application and re-file within the stated period; if the registration is rejected for insufficiency, file a fresh application with the missing attachments and pay any new registration tariff; if an incorrect registered purpose appears, apply for an amendment of the registered purpose.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Customs User Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic portal and the competent district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the corporate register extract, apply to the National Tax Service for the business registration certificate through HomeTax within one month of the commencement of business. Enter the corporate registration number, corporate name, head office address, representative director, business purpose and tax representative details under the categories relevant to customs clearance and logistics support. The district tax office will assign the corporation taxpayer identification number for corporate income tax, value added tax and wage withholding. After tax registration, register the same business owner number with the Korea Customs Service under the UNI-PASS portal and update the customs user profile. This step is mandatory before the customs clearance brokerage application can be considered.
required_dossiers: Certified corporate register extract
Corporate seal certificate
Application for business registration
Power of attorney and identification of the tax representative
Lease agreement for the registered office
Customs user profile registration data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests supporting documents, upload an explanation within the statutory period through HomeTax; if the business type code is queried, re-file with the exact ISIC 5229 description; if the VAT registration fails due to address defects, provide the completed building occupancy certificate and re-apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs Brokerage License and Operational Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Customs Service, principal customs office having jurisdiction over the customs broker workplace, via the UNI-PASS electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: To operate as a customs clearance brokerage house, the corporation must hold a customs clearance business license or employ and register a licensed customs broker under the Customs Act. Submit the application to the principal customs office through UNI-PASS or in writing, including the business registration certificate, certified corporate register extract, company seal certificate, evidence that at least one qualified licensed customs broker is a statutory officer or employee, a floor plan of the customs document office, a confidentiality policy plan, and a security certification for broker-computer access to automated broker interface ACH and wire settlement systems. The customs office reviews the integrity of the corporation, the fitness of the licensed customs broker, and the capability to handle export and import declarations, bonded transit, customs valuations and drawback. Upon approval, the customs authority assigns a broker-specific automation user code and authorizes electronic customs submissions.
required_dossiers: Customs brokerage license application form
Business registration certificate
Certified corporate register extract
Corporate seal certificate
Licensed customs broker qualification certificate and employment contract
Office floor plan and lease agreement
Information security and confidentiality compliance statement
Proof of a bank account linked to the customs electronic settlement system
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the principal customs office suspends the application, provide the missing broker employment certificate or lease confirmation; if the licensed customs broker is deemed insufficient, hire an additional licensed broker and re-file; if the automation interface security certificate is rejected, upgrade the electronic filing system and undergo the customs information security review again.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Korea Customs Service, Office of Customs Broker Licensing, and the municipal government of the registered office for occupancy and fire permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Clearance Brokerage Business License and Customs Broker Automation User Account under Article 113 of the Customs Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - ISIC 5229 is an office-based professional logistics support activity and is not an ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing facility; no environmental impact assessment registration, environmental permission or emission cap is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the facility will not discharge wastewater, emit volatile organic compounds or generate hazardous waste; if bonded transit warehousing is later added, the operator must classify the warehouse under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and comply with the Water Environment Conservation Act effluent standards before operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must obtain a certificate of fire safety for business premises from the local fire department and an occupancy permit certificate issued by the municipal building authority. The fire inspection covers automatic fire alarms, extinguishers, emergency exit signs and, where the floor area exceeds 1,000 square meters, a sprinkler system that meets the Building Code and the Installation, Maintenance and Safety Control of Firefighting Facilities Standards. The employer must file an occupational health and safety declaration with the Ministry of Employment and Labor and submit a workplace safety checklist when hiring employees; if customs records are stored below-grade, the office must also satisfy egress and flood protection requirements under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: Home Tax Service (Hometax) at hometax.go.kr. Customs clearance and brokerage licensing authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity incorporating a Chusik Hoesa, the sole national tax identifier is the Business Registration Number (BRN) issued by the National Tax Service. Procedure: (1) complete corporate registration with the competent Korea court registry; the NTS corporate taxpayer file is then activated. (2) File a business registration application through the Hometax electronic portal or the local tax office using the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, foreign ownership/parent documentation, place-of-business lease, and, if the entity has no Korean fixed establishment, a tax representative appointment. (3) NTS issues the 10-digit BRN and Business Registration Certificate; the same BRN functions as the corporate income tax identification number and VAT registration number. (4) Because the entity is a customs clearance brokerage house, it must additionally obtain the statutory customs brokerage license from Korea Customs Service and register in UNI-PASS as a customs declaration filer. No separate VAT ID is issued; the BRN is statutorily conclusive for direct tax, VAT, withholding, and customs reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in the manner of a U.S. check-the-box election. A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxable as a Korean domestic stock corporation. The only corporate election available in the ordinary course is Korean consolidated tax return filing for a wholly owned domestic subsidiary under the Corporate Tax Act; no pass-through or hybrid mismatch pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value Added Tax Act, administered by the National Tax Service with export-related customs data supplied by the Korea Customs Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no annual turnover threshold for a Chusik Hoesa; any corporation engaged in taxable business supply in South Korea must obtain a Business Registration Number and register for VAT. The simplified taxpayer turnover threshold of KRW 80 million per year applies only to individual small businesses and does not apply to a stock corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registered VAT vendors are required to issue electronic tax invoices and transmit them to the National Tax Information System through Hometax or an approved certified ASP within the statutory deadline; the system is not a continuous real-time fiscal clearance block-stamping model but is a mandatory digital transmission/anti-fraud reporting regime. For exports, the export declaration must be cleared through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS, and the zero-rated e-tax invoice must be linked to the export clearance and reported separately in the periodic VAT return. No analogue paper stamping is required; anti-fraud integrity is achieved by NTS and KCS data cross-matching.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Korean VAT law, 0% VAT applies to exported goods where physical export is proven by a customs export declaration and the proceeds are earned in foreign exchange. Statutory zero-rating also covers services performed outside Korea, international carriage, and other goods/services prescribed by the Value Added Tax Act and Enforcement Decree as supplied for use or consumption outside the Republic of Korea. A licensed customs brokerage may substantiate zero-rating in respect of qualifying export-linked services only when the statutory evidence demonstrates a clear foreign-bound transaction and foreign-exchange earning.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Bill of Entry equivalent) with clearance number
Bill of Lading (ocean freight) or Air Waybill (airfreight)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank foreign exchange settlement confirmation
Proof of foreign exchange acquisition or export proceeds report showing receipt of overseas payment
Customs broker's export clearance statement when filing is performed by the brokerage house
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is accepted only when the mandatory documentation bundle is retained and the export proceeds are repatriated in accordance with Korean foreign exchange rules. If NTS or KCS determines that the zero-rating is unsupported, false, or not related to an actual export, the VAT at 10% is re-assessed with interest and punitive additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including enhanced penalties for false tax invoices and fraudulent refund claims. Criminal sanctions, including imprisonment and fines under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, apply to deliberately fraudulent export zero-rating or refund schemes. NTS may retrospectively claw back refunds within the extended statute of limitations applicable to fraud, and the entity's customs brokerage license may be suspended or revoked by Korea Customs Service for repeat non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a materially liberalized but tightly monitored foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA). Current account transactions, including cross-border service fees, customs brokerage commissions, trade settlement amounts, and dividends, are generally convertible freely through authorized foreign exchange banks. Capital account transactions, by contrast, require either ex ante reporting, declaration, or in certain cases approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the Bank of Korea. A customs brokerage house receiving cross-border commercial payments must ensure that the remittance advice states the proper purpose of payment code to avoid being classified as a capital transaction. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds; earnings may be retained in foreign currency accounts, but the underlying export or service contract must be presented to the settlement bank. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permissible upon submission of audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and the foreign investment report. Practical hurdles include strict real-name financial transaction rules, enhanced due diligence for medium-risk licensed entities, and bank compliance departments requiring clear evidence that the broker is operating under its customs brokerage license rather than as an undisclosed payment intermediary.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds and deemed export service revenue must be collected within 90 days from the date of the export declaration or the date the service is completed, unless an extension is granted by the authorized foreign exchange bank. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into Korean won; 100% of proceeds may be held in a designated foreign currency account. The customs broker or exporter must submit a Foreign Exchange Settlement Report to the settlement bank, and funds must be received in Korea within the statutory timeline to avoid administrative fines and compliance penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Cross-Border Settlement Account and Customs Duty Escrow Account
Foreign Currency Account and KRW Operating Account
Operational Current Account and Bonded Customs Guarantee Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Legal viability for offshore digital EMI is Low. South Korea maintains a traditional bank-centric payments architecture; only domestic banks and narrow-purpose fintech licensees under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act may provide settlement services in Korean won. A non-resident EMI without a domestic banking license cannot directly hold corporate won-denominated accounts or clear customs duty payments through the Korea Customs Service Automated Broker Interface. At best, an EMI could act as an unregulated payment instruction layer via a sponsored bank partnership, but leading Korean banks generally prohibit virtual accounts or umbrella settlement structures for licensed customs brokers. The recommended path is to open Tier-1 domestic bank accounts and use SWIFT MT103 for cross-border receipts rather than relying on EMIs.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch attendance with real-name identification is mandatory for the statutory director or a formally authorized representative under the Financial Transactions Reports Act and the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act. Remote consular notarization can support but does not replace the bank's face-to-face identification for corporate account activation. For non-resident statutory directors, Korean banks typically require an in-branch interview by the director or by a locally resident registered director holding a Korean alien registration card. Power-of-attorney signing authority can be granted only after the initial account opening identity process has been completed and the bank compliance committee has cleared the relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of third-party payments by a customs broker that are not matched to specific goods movement events.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs Brokerage License issued by the Korea Customs Service, a granular monthly settlement ledger mapping each Korean won duty payment to a customs declaration number, import and export contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, customs fee schedules, and an AML self-questionnaire describing the fee-per-declaration model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners with complex shareholding structures or perceived nominee risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate documents including business registration certificate, articles of incorporation, final shareholder registry, signed beneficial ownership declaration, passport copies and foreign registration cards, apostilled certificate of incorporation from the parent jurisdiction, and a reference letter from an existing foreign bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border remittances from or to parties exposed to sanctions, restricted goods, or embargoed trade industries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC and UN sanctions screening outputs, full commercial contracts, proforma invoices, tax identification numbers, Korean customs export control classifications, licenses and end-user certificates, plus sworn statements that shipments comply with trade sanctions legislation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual initial capital injection from a related party that appears to overstate paid-in capital relative to operational needs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds packet including 12 months of overseas corporate bank statements, equity subscription agreement, loan agreement, audited financial statements of the shareholder, evidence of corporate tax residency, and the Bank of Korea foreign investment report or purchase-of-rights certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection for equity must be routed through an authorized foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 or MT202. The Korean entity must submit a Foreign Exchange Declaration and report foreign investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act using the appropriate purpose code for capital contribution. For shareholder loans, registration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act is required. Funds are credited to a Capital Escrow Account and verified against the reported investment amount. After receipt, the bank issues a certificate of foreign exchange purchase or import of foreign currency, and the company registers paid-in capital with the relevant Korean registration court. Supporting contracts, invoices, board resolutions, and statutory audit reports must be retained for at least five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Customs duties and bonded warehouse fees are paid in Korean won through the Korea Customs Service Automated Broker Interface using domestic wire; cross-border disbursements to foreign carriers, overseas surveyors, or non-resident service providers are cleared by SWIFT MT103, commercial letters of credit, or documentary collections. For each outgoing MT103, the remitter must state the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code and attach underlying trade documentation. Standing instructions and batch payment schedules should be avoided; every disbursement must be traceable to a specific monthly customs clearance statement or bonded transit management event.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Domestic Korean won and US dollar forward contracts for booked trade and service receivables or payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) available through the Seoul interbank market only upon proof of underlying export or import exposure
Currency swaps limited to current-account trade flows and prohibited for speculative capital arbitrage

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and year-end accounting settlement statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31 of the following calendar year; if the company is subject to mandatory external audit, the statutory filing window is extended to May 31; for non-calendar fiscal year-ends, within 3 months (or 5 months if externally audited) after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or false corporate tax return attracts a 20% unfiled-return penalty on the payable tax, a 10% understated-return penalty on the understated amount, and 0.022% daily late-payment interest; persistent non-filing can lead to asset seizure, compulsory collection, closure of the business registration, and court-ordered dissolution of the company as a dormant corporation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surtax return and payment to the competent local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal / provincial tax authorities through the NTS HomeTax integrated local income tax module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The same deadline as the annual corporate income tax return; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, March 31 (or May 31 if subject to mandatory external audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or understated local income tax surtax attracts a 10% to 20% unfaithful-return penalty plus 0.022% daily interest for non-payment; continued delinquency triggers asset seizure and local-government compulsory execution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' general meeting, approval of financial statements, and preparation of the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records retained at the registered office and subject to inspection by the National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service; related director or share-change registrations are filed with the Commercial Registration Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the ordinary general meeting may result in administrative fines for directors under the Korean Commercial Act; repeated failure may be treated as corporate inactivity and support an administrative strike-off or court dissolution for a dormant company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external audit report submission to the statutory financial supervisory system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) through the electronic external audit reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external auditor must file the completed audit report within 10 days of audit completion; the company must ensure the audited financial statements are finally approved by the ordinary shareholders' meeting within 3 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor when required, or failure to file the audit report, can invalidate the statutory audit, expose the company to regulatory fines, suspend the customs brokerage license until remediation, and may cause criminal penalties for responsible directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual customs brokerage business performance report and license maintenance return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS) — the regional customs office with jurisdiction over the company's registered office or the Korea Customs Broker Association as required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the end of each business year, not later than February 28 for a December 31 fiscal year-end unless a formal extension is granted by the Korea Customs Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false filing may trigger a warning, a suspension of the customs brokerage license for up to one year, revocation of the license for repeated or serious violations, and administrative fines; while suspended, the company may not lawfully provide customs clearance brokerage or bonded transit services

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership change notice and customs brokerage controlling-shareholder confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Customs Service and National Tax Service under the customs license and tax registration framework
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any transfer resulting in a 10% or greater change of shares or voting rights must be reported to the Korea Customs Service within 30 days; a corresponding amendment to the tax business registration and commercial register must be filed within the Korean statutory event-window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-notification may be treated as breach of the customs brokerage licensing conditions and can trigger license suspension, revocation, and monetary penalties; the underlying share transfer remains valid, but the company loses compliance certification status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Chusik Hoesa legally requires an independent certified public accountant audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if any of the following quantitative thresholds is satisfied at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end: (i) balance-sheet trigger: total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million); (ii) turnover trigger: total annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 75.0 million); (iii) headcount trigger: full-time headcount equals or exceeds 300 employees and total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.3 million); (iv) the company is listed, has publicly offered securities, or is a financial services or public-interest entity designated by the Financial Services Commission; or (v) the Korea Customs Service requires an audit as a licensing condition for the customs brokerage or bonded transit management licence
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for mandatory external audit targets and listed companies; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for non-audit-target private companies; small companies may apply the Korean Small and Medium Enterprise Accounting Standards if qualification criteria are met. Customs brokerage records must be reconciled to the Automated Broker Interface ACH accounting records and the Korea Customs Service electronic declaration system.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not operate a public annual UBO return for private Chusik Hoesa companies. The annual confirmation is achieved through the corporate tax return and financial statement disclosures to the National Tax Service, the annual customs brokerage performance report to the Korea Customs Service, and the required on-site statutory registers. Any share transfer or controlling-ownership change of 10% or more of issued shares or voting rights must be reported to the Korea Customs Service within 30 days, and the Register of Members must be updated promptly. Foreign-investment events must be reported to the relevant Korean authority through the integrated foreign investment monitoring system if the foreign ownership threshold is triggered.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,500 per year for a standard Seoul registered office and corporate secretarial agent; USD 1,200 - USD 2,500 per year if the service includes a resident director or customs-license nominee support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 25,000 for a mandatory external audit of a non-listed customs brokerage Chusik Hoesa under K-IFRS; smaller scope may range USD 6,000 - USD 12,000 if the audit is conducted under K-GAAP

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (top progressive rate applicable to taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays and preferential Free Economic Zone incentives under the Special Act on Designation and Management of Free Economic Zones (100% corporate income tax exemption for the first 3-5 years and 50% reduction for the following 2 years for qualifying foreign-invested enterprises); R&D tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (up to 30-40% of qualifying R&D expenditure); income tax exemption for new growth engine and patented technology commercialization income (30-100%); additional presumptive payroll and employment credits; no general patent box regime but specific technology transfer income exemption applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax and Tax Base Return (Corporate Tax Return Form 1) filed through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end, i.e., 31 March for calendar-year corporations; foreign corporations with no domestic place of business file within 6 months after fiscal year-end; an extension of up to 1 month is available upon approval per Corporate Income Tax Act Article 12-13.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, legal name of the Chusik Hoesa, registered head office address, representative director details, and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact legal name as registered on the corporate registration certificate. For non-resident representative directors or executive officers, provide passport number and overseas residential address; if a director holds a Korean alien registration card, input that number. Attach a shareholder schedule listing non-resident shareholders, their jurisdiction of tax residence, percentage ownership, and any claimed treaty status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from customs clearance brokerage, bonded transit management, warehouse handling, freight forwarding, logistics consulting, and other operating income; corresponding cost of sales and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income on an accrual basis under K-IFRS. All intercompany revenue and expenses must be recognised at arm's length; if the customs brokerage transacts with a foreign affiliate, attach a reconciliation schedule showing transfer pricing adjustments. Non-resident owned companies must ensure that management fees paid abroad are supported by verifiable documentation evidencing actual service delivery.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs of non-deductible expenses (excessive entertainment, fines, penalties, political donations, reserves exceeding legal limits) and deductions of non-taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges for home-office support services or royalty payments to non-residents must satisfy the economic substance and expenditure-benefit tests; otherwise, the NTS will disallow the deduction and impose a 10-40% unfaithful return penalty. If a foreign parent is invoicing for brokerage-related software, the software payments may be re-characterised as royalties subject to withholding tax and possible treaty limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Base and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculated after deducting brought-forward tax losses; In Korea, net operating losses may be carried forward for 10 years for domestic corporations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses arising from foreign branches are generally not offsetable against Korean-source income absent a treaty participation clause. A change-in-shareholding of 50% or more does not extinguish carryforward losses of the Chusik Hoesa, but a failure to submit the statutory carryforward schedule, loss-history, and foreign loss reconciliation with the return will result in disallowance. Non-resident investors must document the loss utilization timeline because excess carryforward can trigger treaty anti-abuse scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Gross Corporate Income Tax at Progressive Rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tentative corporate income tax by applying progressive rates: 10% up to KRW 200 million; 20% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 22% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 25% on the excess above KRW 300 billion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The progressive rate table is applied identically to domestic and foreign-owned corporations; Free Economic Zone tax holiday companies must attach the approval certificate from the relevant tax office and recompute the reduced amount. If the NTS has previously issued a revised assessment, disclose the subsequent adjustment in the reconciliation box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible tax credits including foreign tax credit, R&D credits, employment incentive credits, investment credits, and statutory exemption/reduction under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The corporation may claim a foreign tax credit for taxes paid on foreign-source income earned through a permanent establishment or branch, subject to treaty limitations. If non-resident shareholders control the board, the R&D credit claim must be substantiated by actual research employee payroll and cost records; any fabricated credit will be recaptured with a 40% fraud penalty and criminal exposure for the directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Net Payable Tax, Local Income Tax Surcharge, and Additional Taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable after credits, plus the 10% local income tax surcharge, late-filing penalties, unfaithful-return additional taxes, and interest/overdue surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All payments must be made in Korean won via HomeTax. The 10% local surtax is assessed on the net corporate income tax, including surcharges; it is not covered by any double tax treaty reduction. Dividend distributions to non-residents must be disclosed in this box as a cross-reference to Box 8, and the withholding agent must remit the statutory 22% dividend withholding tax within the prescribed monthly payment deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees paid or credited to non-resident shareholders or foreign affiliates, together with the withholding tax amount, treaty rate claimed, and beneficial ownership declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the 'Withholding under Tax Treaties' schedule and Form for Application for Non-resident Tax Exemption/Reduction under Bilateral Tax Treaties. Each foreign payee must supply a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty partner tax authority and a current beneficial ownership declaration. If the payee is a shell or conduit entity without actually carrying on business, the treaty benefit is denied and the full 22% withholding tax becomes payable from the Korean payer, with penalties for failure to withhold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return, without a proper extension, attracts a penalty equal to 20% of the unpaid tax if no return is filed (Framework Act on National Taxes Article 75-2). An understated return triggers an additional tax of 10% of the understated amount, escalating to 40% when the understatement is fraudulent or deliberately hidden. Non-payment or late payment of the assessed corporate tax incurs a daily surcharge at 0.022% per day (and an additional interest surcharge during economic shock periods). The Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (Article 8) authorises imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax for intentional evasion; for licensed customs brokerages, the Korea Customs Service may simultaneously revoke the customs brokerage licence under the Customs Act and blacklist the representative director from conducting customs business for up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% dividend withholding tax under the Corporate/Income Tax Act plus 10% local income surtax on the withholding tax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke bilateral double tax treaty (DTA) relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident recipient must be the beneficial owner of the income and present a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction. The Korean payer must file, before payment, an 'Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaty' (foreign corporation schedule) with the National Tax Service through HomeTax, attaching a current TRC, a detailed ownership chart, board meeting minutes authorising the income distribution, audited financial statements or substance evidence of the recipient, and a declaration that the recipient is not a conduit arrangement within Article 4 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. The NTS generally processes the application within 14 days and will issue a certificate of approval; the withholding agent must remit the reduced rate. If treaty relief is claimed without the TRC, or if beneficial ownership cannot be substantiated, the withholding agent must withhold the full 22% and the payee may subsequently file a domestic refund claim with supporting documents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate for outbound royalties to non-residents is 22% (20% plus 10% local surtax) on gross Korean-source royalties; statutory rate for outbound interest is also 22% (20% plus 10% local surtax). DTA rates vary by jurisdiction: for example, under the Korea-US treaty, interest may be reduced to 10% (and 0% for certain banking interest) and royalties to 15% (or 10% for industrial equipment royalties); under the Korea-UK treaty, interest is reduced to 10%, royalties to 10% (0% for marine/air transport royalties), while the Korea-OECD Model template generally provides for 5-10% dividend rates, 10% interest, and 0-15% royalties. Claimants must follow the same treaty-application protocol with TRC, beneficial owner form, and anti-abuse declaration.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million) of aggregate cross-border intercompany transactions (including sales of goods, provision of services, loans, royalties, and brokerage commissions) in a fiscal year triggers the simultaneous preparation and submission of the Local File and Master File under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA); simplified documentation may apply to small and medium enterprises with intercompany transactions below KRW 5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not impose a separate Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) in the style of the UAE, but the substance-over-form principle is codified in Article 14(3) of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 4(1) of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. The National Tax Service may disregard artificial entities, re-characterise transactions, and deny treaty benefits where the non-resident counterparty lacks core income-generating activities (CIGA) in its own jurisdiction. A licensed customs brokerage house operating in Korea must have local management and decision-making, bank accounts, ACH/automated broker interface systems, personnel, and physical office substance; failure to maintain such substance while declaring dividends or royalties to a tax-haven or low-tax affiliate may result in the assignment of the income to the Korean entity, full 22% withholding, and an understatement penalty of up to 40%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting cash-based customs brokerage fees from the taxable income, issuing false VAT invoices for fictitious bonded transit management services, inflating operating expenses, or using undisclosed foreign bank accounts to conceal revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Article 8(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act; imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax; additional corporate tax of 40% of the understated amount for false or fraudulent return under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3; automatic revocation of the customs brokerage licence under the Customs Act and prohibition from re-registration for 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced under the Korean Commercial Act Article 389(3) read together with Article 210 where directors have acted in bad faith or with gross negligence; directors who planned, encouraged, or executed the evasion become jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and damages. The director may be placed on a travel ban (departure restriction) for tax debts exceeding KRW 100 million, blacklisted by the National Tax Service and Korea Customs, and, upon criminal conviction, imprisoned for up to 5 years and disqualified from serving as a director or customs broker executive for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing customs clearance and logistics services to a related foreign parent or affiliate at an artificial low margin, paying excessive consultancy fees to an affiliate with no actual economic substance, or allocating cross-border costs/commissions in a way that erodes the Korean tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 5 and 6 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA) authorise the NTS to make an arm's-length adjustment; the additional tax is 20% of the adjusted taxable income, increased to 40% where the return is dishonest or a sham transaction is found; interest surcharge of 0.75% per month on the cash-settled extended tax. In flagrant cases, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is invoked for fraudulent profit shifting with criminal sanctions of up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign intercompany pricing agreements without conducting an arm's-length analysis or who approve circular financial flows are treated as active participants in the tax offence; they are personally liable for the corrected corporate tax under the doctrine of substance-over-form and can face civil restitution to the company for loss of assets. After the NTS issues a corrective assessment, the unpaid amount creates a director travel ban; if criminal, directors may be jailed for up to 5 years and can be blocked from operating any licensed customs activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Shell Company and AML/CTF Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Chusik Hoesa as a shell/ conduit corporation to channel overseas funds for customs duty payments without real business activity, structuring wire or Automated Broker Interface (ACI) payments to defeat the Financial Transactions Reports Act reporting threshold of KRW 10 million, or failing to report suspicious transactions connected to bonded transit cargo to the Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Article 27(1) of the Financial Transactions Reports Act; imprisonment of up to 5 years and a criminal fine not exceeding KRW 50 million; violation of customs bonding regulations under the Customs Act Articles 270-274 triggers at least KRW 10 million in fines and revocation of the customs brokerage licence; any profit derived from the implicated brokerage transactions is subject to confiscation; corporate penalties reach 20% of the transaction amounts in additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts will disregard the shell entity and attribute the smuggling, money-laundering, or duty-evading conduct to the natural-person directors because a corporate shell cannot itself perform customs brokerage; directors are jointly liable for customs duties, VAT, penalties, and criminal restitution. The director will be blacklisted by KoFIU and the Korea Customs Service, prohibited from travelling abroad while the criminal case is pending, and, if convicted, sentenced to up to 5 years imprisonment; a second or organized-crime enhanced conviction can double the sentence. The constitutional and commercial law 'limited liability' shield is expressly void where the company is a façade and the director has acted in a self-interested or knowingly fraudulent manner.
